vulnerabilities: Limited strategic munition and stockpile depth — industrial base optimized for high-technology production rather than sustained high-rate conventional attrition warfare, risking rapid depletion of precision-guided munitions during initial conflict weeks

Erosion of traditional influence infrastructure in Africa — loss of forward military basing and diplomatic backing in the Sahel as Russia and China sponsor regional counter-alignments, with uranium-sourcing risk
Fiscal deficit and public debt pressures constraining long-term military budget expansion

Vulnerability of scattered Indo-Pacific overseas territories (La Réunion, New Caledonia, French Polynesia) — limited self-defence assets against gray-zone tactics or political destabilisation campaigns
Dependence on foreign critical minerals and raw materials (largely Chinese-processed) for high-tech industrial and defence manufacturing
strengths: Independent sovereign nuclear triad (air/submarine) — Triomphant-class SSBNs with M51 SLBMs, entirely free from foreign operational veto
World's second-largest Exclusive Economic Zone via global overseas territories across the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans
Comprehensive sovereign defence industrial base — domestic capability to build fighter aircraft (Rafale), nuclear submarines, and missile systems without foreign dependency
Permanent UN Security Council veto combined with EU strategic leadership
Nuclear energy infrastructure autonomy — over 60% of domestic power from nuclear reactors, insulating against fossil-fuel shocks
